title: Dissipation driven boundary localization in higher order topological insulators
authors: Xue Ping Ren, Xiao Ran Wang, Xin Ran Ma, Xi Hu, Su Peng Kou
abstract: We study dissipation driven boundary localization in a Bernevig Hughes Zhang type second order topological insulator by introducing inhomogeneous, spin dependent boundary dissipation. After projection onto the edge subspace, the dominant component of the boundary dissipation lies in the same Pauli channel as the kinetic term. This channel gives both counter-propagating edge modes the same real transfer exponent. The two modes therefore accumulate at the same dissipative domain wall. For the corner states, the dissipative envelope competes with Jackiw Rebbi localization. Increasing dissipation moves their weight from the geometric corners to the dissipative domain wall. Propagating edge states also localize at this wall. Numerical calculations confirm the qualitative predictions of the edge theory. A fixed energy Feshbach reduction captures finite size effects. Inhomogeneous boundary dissipation thus controls boundary state localization without changing the bulk topology.
summary: This work analyzes how engineered dissipation controls boundary state localization in higher-order topological insulators. By projecting the system onto the edge subspace, the authors show that the dissipation couples uniformly to both edge modes, forcing them to localize together at a common dissipative domain wall. This mechanism offers a topological control knob for boundary physics without modifying the bulk band structure.
main_problem: The study investigates how engineered boundary dissipation affects the localization of edge and corner states in Higher-Order Topological Insulators (HOTIs).
main_result: The dominant boundary dissipation couples to the kinetic term, causing both counter-propagating edge modes to localize at the same dissipative domain wall, which controls state localization without altering the bulk topology.
method: The analysis employs projection onto the edge subspace, utilizing boundary transfer theory and fixed-energy Feshbach reduction techniques.
model_or_system: The model is a Bernevig–Hughes–Zhang-type second-order topological insulator (SOTI) lattice, perturbed by inhomogeneous, spin-dependent boundary dissipation ($\delta H$).
key_observables: Edge state localization, corner state weight distribution, and the real transfer exponent ($\lambda_\pm$).
important_parameters: Dissipation strength ($\gamma_e(\ell)$), effective edge mass ($m_e(\ell)$), and the energy $E$.
main_assumptions: The effective Hamiltonian is assumed valid when dissipation and mass terms are small compared to the bulk gap energy.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian and projecting to the edge subspace, developing the transfer theory for edge states, analyzing the zero-energy limit, and concluding with numerical confirmation of the localization mechanism.
why_interesting: The concept of dissipation controlling topological boundary physics is highly relevant to open quantum systems, as it provides a mechanism to engineer boundary behavior in systems where dissipation is unavoidable.
